solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Carry around old copper valve

indicators.note: around tells us the word for carry wraps itself about the other pieces

parts.note: a shop that carries a line has it in stock
PC, police constable, is slang for a copper

explanation.surface: Someone is told to bring an old copper valve along with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry' reads as an instruction to transport something, but it gives a noun: what a shop carries is its stock.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tap or valve fitted in a pipe to shut off the flow of water or gas.

clue.text: Poles from south added to workforce

indicators.note: added to says the letter for south is attached to the end of the word for workforce

parts.note: a firm's staff is its workforce
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Polish workers coming up from the south join a company's workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' tempts you to read it as people from Poland, but here it means long sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffs are long walking sticks or rods, so they are poles in the plain sense of the word.

clue.text: Learner rode a kicking mare

indicators.note: a kicking animal thrashes about, so the letters of rode and a are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
L is the learner plate on a car

explanation.surface: A beginner rider sits on a mare that is kicking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kicking' scrambles RODE A to ORDEA, which goes after L. 'Mare' is British slang, short for nightmare: a horrible experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare, short for nightmare, is a draining and unpleasant experience, which is what an ordeal is.

clue.text: Animal doctor invested in remedy for large erection

parts.note: a cat is an animal

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the doctor goes within the word for remedy

parts.note: to heal is to remedy

explanation.surface: A vet puts money into a cure for impotence, a large erection.
explanation.walkthrough: The innuendo of 'large erection' hides a building: something erected. 'Invested in' means placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge church built as the seat of a bishop is literally a large structure that has been put up.

clue.text: Protected food from my horrors, catching one son noshing apple cores

parts.note: cor, like my, is an exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: catching means the word for horrors holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: nasties are horrible things, as in video nasties
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the cores of the two words are their middle letters

explanation.surface: A child munching apple cores is somehow protected from some awful dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters of NOSHING and APPLE are H and P; with IS they go inside NASTIES after its N. 'Protected' refers to the pasty's legally protected regional status in the EU and UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasties from Cornwall have protected geographical status, so only ones made there can carry the name.

clue.text: Complex way to kill conversation

definitions.meaning: a psychological complex is a neurotic fixation or inhibition
putting the phone down ends a call abruptly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Complex' is a noun here, a psychological fixation, not the adjective meaning complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurotic inhibition is a psychological complex, and replacing the receiver ends a phone conversation.

clue.text: Taking off with a resonant sound

parts.note: a ping is a short ringing sound

explanation.surface: An aircraft takes off with a ringing noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' suggests a plane leaving the ground, but it means imitating someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic them, just as aping means copying someone's behaviour.

clue.text: Adults fill bodies with wine regularly

indicators.note: fill tells us the picked letters go inside the word for bodies

parts.note: groups are bodies of people

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of wine

explanation.surface: Grown people stuff themselves with wine on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bodies' means groups of people, not physical bodies being filled.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown-ups is the informal word for adults, used especially by and to children.

clue.text: Power nap for bed-hopping politician

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power

indicators.note: hopping means the bed jumps into the word for nap

parts.note: a nap is a rest
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: A womanising politician needs a power nap.
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott was the UK's Deputy Prime Minister whose affair made headlines, which 'bed-hopping' hints at; here 'hopping' moves a bed into a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: John Prescott was a senior British Labour politician and Deputy Prime Minister under Tony Blair.

clue.text: Preposterous — one council bans dashes

indicators.note: dashes is a verb here: it smashes the letters, which are then rearranged

explanation.surface: An outrageous move: a local council bans the punctuation dash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashes' reads as punctuation marks being banned, but it is a verb, smashing up ONE COUNCIL BANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unreasonable or beyond what conscience allows is outrageous, close to preposterous.

clue.text: Foreign car's rubbish, recalled examiner

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the word for rubbish is turned around

parts.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: An imported car is so poor it has been recalled by the maker for an examination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' sounds like a manufacturer's recall, but it reverses ROT to TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor is someone who examines accounts, so an inspector or examiner of books.

clue.text: Performing moonies is offensive

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are putting on an act, rearranged into a new show

explanation.surface: Members of the Moonies cult putting on a show is offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Moonies is a nickname for members of the Unification Church.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpleasant to the senses, especially a foul smell, is noisome, i.e. offensive.

clue.text: Female by pool shaving

parts.note: a lake is a large pool of water

explanation.surface: A woman shaves beside a swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaving' looks like an action but is a noun: a thin sliver.
explanation.definitionFit: A flake is a thin sliver, like a shaving pared off wood or chocolate.

clue.text: Non-vital half of company taken over by American one

indicators.note: a firm taken over by another sits inside it, so the half goes inside the American company

parts.note: Inc is the US abbreviation for an incorporated company, an American one

indicators.note: half of means only the first six letters of the twelve-letter word are used

parts.note: an organisation is a company

explanation.surface: Half of a company is non-essential and gets bought by a US firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-vital' looks like unimportant, but means not living. The company halved is ORGANISATION, cut to its first six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inorganic matter is not derived from living things, so it is literally lacking life.

clue.text: Without confusion, organise unfinished playing area

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the confusion is surrounded
unfinished means the last letter of the word for organise is dropped

parts.note: to orchestrate a thing is to organise it
pi or pie is printers' jumbled type, a state of confusion

explanation.surface: Calmly organise a half-completed playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, and 'Without confusion' is not 'calmly'. 'Unfinished' trims the last letter, giving ORCHESTRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The sunken area in front of a stage where musicians play is where the orchestra sits.

clue.text: Drug blocking tear and crying reflex

indicators.note: blocking says the drug sits inside the tear, obstructing it

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip
E is short for ecstasy
to rant is to cry out loudly

explanation.surface: A drug stops tears and weeping, a reflex reaction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear' is pronounced as a rip here, not as a drop from the eye. 'Reflex' refers to a reflex angle.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a re-entrant angle points inwards, being greater than 180 degrees, i.e. a reflex angle.

clue.text: More pies to be cooked, one's assured

indicators.note: pies to be cooked are prepared, so the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone is given a guarantee that more pies will be baked.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'one's assured' as one who is assured, the person given a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: The person to whom a promise is made, who has been given an assurance, is the legal term here.

clue.text: Canine upset ambassador, biting the old fart

indicators.note: biting means the ambassador's letters hold the other pieces between them
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
ye is an old form of the
toot is slang for breaking wind

explanation.surface: A dog bites and offends an ambassador who has just passed wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' looks like a dog, but is a tooth. HE turned upside down is EH, which holds YE TOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed canine teeth in the upper jaw are also called eye teeth.

clue.text: Naval division from Mary Rose lain at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The Mary Rose, Henry VIII's warship, has lain on the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mary Rose is a Tudor warship that sank in 1545 and was raised in 1982.
explanation.definitionFit: The marines are the Royal Navy's amphibious infantry corps, a division of the naval service.

clue.text: Game even includes duck

indicators.note: includes means the duck sits inside the word for even

parts.note: being quits means being even, with nothing owed
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: An evenly matched game allows a duck in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of nothing, hence the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a throwing game in which rings are tossed over a peg.

clue.text: Weapon disembowelled warlord

indicators.note: having its innards removed means the middle letter of the weapon is taken out

parts.note: a shotgun is a weapon

explanation.surface: A warlord gutted with a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOTGUN has seven letters; removing its middle T leaves SHOGUN.
explanation.definitionFit: The shoguns were hereditary military rulers of Japan, warlords governing in the emperor's name.

clue.text: Worn-out old lady doesn't finish before a late hour

indicators.note: not finishing means the last letter of the word for old lady is dropped

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother
ten o'clock is a late hour

explanation.surface: A tired old woman can't finish her task before a late hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old lady' is British slang for mother; 'doesn't finish' drops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes damaged by moths are tattered and shabby, so worn out or obsolete.

clue.text: Mirror repositioned partially reflecting boob

indicators.note: reflecting says the hidden letters are read backwards
partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mirror put in the wrong place is a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: RORRE sits across mirROR REpositioned and reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Boob is British slang for a silly blunder or mistake.

clue.text: Back pain without sign of timeout, that's reality

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the reversed pain wraps around
back means the word for pain is read backwards

parts.note: to hurt is to cause pain; hurt is pain

indicators.note: the sign of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Back pain with no break to rest: that is reality.
explanation.walkthrough: HURT reversed is TRUH, which goes around T, the first letter of timeout.
explanation.definitionFit: Truth is the state of things as they really are, so it means reality or fact.

clue.text: Whip company overwhelmed by sudden rush

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means the company is swamped, inside the word for sudden rush

parts.note: a surge is a sudden rush forward

explanation.surface: A party whip finds a company engulfed by a sudden rush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' suggests a parliamentary party whip, but it is the instrument of punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip used for punishment, and to scourge is to flog.

clue.text: Intense series ends in striking fashion

indicators.note: in places the ends of the series inside the striking fashion

parts.note: bling is flashy, eye-catching jewellery and dress
the alphabet series runs from A to Z, its two ends

explanation.surface: An intense TV series finishes in striking style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Series ends' are the ends of the alphabet series, A and Z, not the last letters of the word 'series'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blazing means burning fiercely, and by extension fierce or intense, as in a blazing row.

clue.text: Urge to blackmail husband for the first time

indicators.note: read as for the first T: the husband replaces the first of the two letters T

parts.note: to extort is to obtain by blackmail

explanation.surface: Someone is encouraged to blackmail a husband for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the first time' means swapping H for the first T of EXTORT, not 'on the first occasion'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to strongly encourage or press someone, which is to urge them.

clue.text: Can joint set after operation?

indicators.note: after an operation things are rearranged, so the letters are put in new order

explanation.surface: Can a broken joint be set after surgery?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb meaning 'is able to', but it is the slang verb meaning to throw away.
explanation.definitionFit: To can something is to scrap or discard it, and jettisoning is throwing cargo or items away.
